content:
Start by treating $k$ as a fixed number and writing the system as a matrix equation:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 1 & k \\
1 & k & 1 \\
k & 1 & 1
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
x \\
y \\
z
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
1 \\
1 \\
1
\end{bmatrix}
$$

The coefficient matrix is the square matrix multiplying the unknowns. Its determinant tells you whether the system has a unique solution: if the determinant is nonzero, the matrix is invertible, so there is exactly one solution.

If the determinant is zero, that test alone can’t tell you whether there are infinitely many solutions or none. Then you check whether the equations are consistent—for example, by row-reducing the coefficient matrix together with the right-hand side.

Your next step: calculate the determinant of the coefficient matrix as an expression in $k$.
